subject: psychology
title: Biopsychology: Localisation & Hemispheric Lateralisation
welcome_lead: Different jobs for different patches of cortex — and two halves that disagree.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology localisation: Broca, Wernicke, motor cortex, hemispheric lateralisation, split-brain.
final_note: Function localises, but plasticity blurs the map.

concepts.def: Specific brain areas have specific functions.
Left frontal lobe area for speech production.
Left temporal lobe area for speech comprehension.
Fibre bridge linking the two hemispheres.

walkthroughs.body_html: Broca (1861) studied 'Tan', who could only say 'tan' but understood speech — damage to a left frontal area. Wernicke (1874) found temporal-lobe damage caused fluent but meaningless speech. The motor cortex (frontal) controls movement; the somatosensory cortex (parietal) processes touch.

Language is left-lateralised in ~95% of right-handers. The right hemisphere is dominant for face recognition and spatial tasks. The corpus callosum carries about 200 million axons between hemispheres.

Sperry (1968) studied 11 patients with severed corpus callosa. Objects shown to the left visual field (right hemisphere) could be drawn but not named; objects in the right visual field (left hemisphere) could be named. Hemispheres genuinely specialise.
